name: 5-phospho-alpha-D-ribose 1-diphosphate
description: Input boundary for de novo nucleotide core biosynthesis.

name: inosine 5'-monophosphate(2-)
description: Purine core boundary connecting core and branch biosynthesis GIFTs.

name: adenosine 5'-monophosphate(2-)
description: Output boundary of adenylate biosynthesis.

name: guanosine 5'-monophosphate(2-)
description: Output boundary that establishes guanylate identity before shared nucleotide phosphorylation.

name: L-glutamine
description: Nitrogen-donor input boundary for de novo pyrimidine core biosynthesis.

name: uridine 5'-monophosphate(2-)
description: Output boundary of de novo pyrimidine core biosynthesis.

name: uridine 5'-triphosphate(4-)
description: Stable uridine nucleotide input immediately before cytidylate-specific amination.

name: cytidine 5'-triphosphate(4-)
description: Output boundary that establishes cytidylate identity.

name: (2R)-3-phosphoglycerate
description: Glycolytic intermediate; the junction where carbon leaves central metabolism for serine biosynthesis.

name: L-serine
description: Stable amino acid product and the precursor of glycine and of both cysteine biosynthesis GIFTs.

name: glycine
description: Output boundary of glycine biosynthesis.

name: L-cysteine
description: Stable amino acid product; also the sulfur-donor input boundary of transsulfuration.

name: hydrogen sulfide
description: Assimilable inorganic sulfur input boundary shared by sulfide-dependent cysteine and methionine biosynthesis.

name: L-aspartate
description: Central amino acid input boundary of the aspartate family.

name: L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde
description: Branchpoint separating the lysine and diaminopimelate branch from the threonine and methionine branch.

name: L-homoserine
description: Branchpoint that commits aspartate carbon to threonine or to methionine.

name: L-threonine
description: Output boundary of threonine biosynthesis.

name: L-methionine
description: Output boundary of methionine biosynthesis.

name: L-homocysteine
description: Input-only sulfur-donor boundary supplied by methionine salvage. Never declared as an output anchor; see the acyclicity note in database_changes.

name: L-fucose
description: Deoxyhexose of host mucin O-glycans and plant cell walls.

name: L-rhamnopyranose
description: Deoxyhexose of pectic rhamnogalacturonan.

name: beta-D-galactose
description: Hexose released from lactose, galactans and host glycans.

name: N-acetyl-D-glucosamine
description: Amino sugar of chitin, peptidoglycan and host glycans.

name: aceneuramate
description: Open form of N-acetylneuraminate (sialic acid), the terminal residue of host mucin O-glycans released by sialidases.

name: D-glucuronate
description: Uronic acid of glucuronoxylan and host glycosaminoglycans.

name: aldehydo-D-galacturonate
description: Uronic acid backbone residue of pectin.

name: D-xylulose 5-phosphate
description: Pentose phosphate pathway entry point for pentose catabolism.

name: beta-D-fructose 6-phosphate
description: Glycolytic entry point for amino sugar catabolism.

name: alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate
description: First stable product of the Leloir pathway, before shared phosphoglucomutase chemistry.

name: dihydroxyacetone phosphate
description: Glycolytic entry point for deoxyhexose catabolism.

name: (S)-lactaldehyde
description: Co-product of deoxyhexose aldol cleavage.

name: pyruvate
description: Central carbon entry point.

name: D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
description: Glycolytic entry point; distinct from the PG3 anchor of serine biosynthesis.

name: D-xylose
description: Pentose released by xylan saccharification, outside the cell.

name: D-xylose
description: D-xylose in the cytoplasm, where isomerase-dependent catabolism begins.

name: L-arabinose
description: Pentose released from arabinan and arabinoxylan side chains, outside the cell.

name: L-arabinose
description: L-arabinose in the cytoplasm, where catabolism begins.

name: arabinoxylan
description: Arabinose-decorated xylan of cereal and grass cell walls; the dominant hemicellulose of a plant-based diet. A substrate class rather than a single compound.

name: xylan
description: Beta-1,4-linked xylose backbone remaining after side-chain removal. A substrate class rather than a single compound.

name: starch
description: Alpha-glucan storage polysaccharide of plants, and the major digestible carbohydrate of most diets.

name: D-glucose
description: Hexose released by alpha-glucosidase. Compartment unresolved: glucose is moved mainly by promiscuous carriers, so no uptake GIFT licenses a split.

name: collagen
description: Fibrillar triple-helical structural protein of animal extracellular matrix, and the most abundant protein of animal tissue. A substrate class rather than a single compound: it has no balanced-equation identity and Rhea represents it as the polymer [collagen].

name: collagen peptides
description: Heterogeneous peptides released by cleavage of the collagen triple helix. Deliberately substrate-specific rather than a shared peptide pool, so that protein-degradation GIFTs do not connect through an undefined intermediate; see inst/doc/proposal-protein-degradation.md.

name: acetyl-CoA
description: Central acyl-CoA branchpoint where sugar, amino acid and fatty acid carbon converge. Declared as a boundary only for the GIFTs listed in gift_anchors; reactions elsewhere that consume acetyl-CoA internally do not gain an edge from it, because gifter derives composition from declared anchors and never from shared reaction participants.

name: acetate
description: Two-carbon fermentation end product, and the CoA acceptor consumed by the butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase route. Compartment unresolved: no SCFA transport GIFT is evidenceable, so the extracellular claim that cross-feeding would need is deliberately not made.

name: butanoate
description: Four-carbon fermentation end product of the acetyl-CoA condensation route. Compartment unresolved, as for acetate.

name: propanoate
description: Three-carbon fermentation end product reached by two curated routes with different inputs. Compartment unresolved, as for acetate.

name: (S)-propane-1,2-diol
description: Reduced product of deoxyhexose aldol cleavage and the input of the propanediol route to propionate. Stereochemistry follows the (S)-lactaldehyde anchor it comes from; the dehydratase reaction RHEA:14569 is stereochemically unspecified in Rhea and is therefore stated at lower specificity than this boundary.

name: (R)-lactate
description: Input-only boundary of the acrylate route to propionate. Never declared as an output anchor: lactate formation is out of scope for this layer, so nothing in gifter produces it and the acyclicity argument is the one already recorded for L-homocysteine.

name: (S)-lactate
description: L-lactate, the enantiomer formed by the NAD-dependent L-lactate dehydrogenase of fermentative Bacillota and Actinomycetota. Declared as a separate anchor from the existing (R)-lactate rather than as a compartment variant of it, because the two are different molecules: the acrylate route to propanoate accepts only the (R) form, and the enzymes that form the two enantiomers are unrelated.

name: (S)-malate
description: Central-carbon boundary produced by the glyoxylate bypass and consumed by malolactic fermentation. It remains internal to fumarate_oxaloacetate_interconversion, so that reaction participant creates no additional edge.

name: citrate
description: Input-only boundary of citrate fermentation. Declared unspecified rather than extracellular because no curated transport GIFT licenses a compartment split; the CitT carrier of the Enterobacteriaceae and the plasmid-borne CitP permease of the lactic acid bacteria are unrelated proteins and neither is curated.

name: ethanol
description: Neutral fermentation end product of the bifunctional acetaldehyde/alcohol dehydrogenase route from acetyl-CoA.

name: (R)-acetoin
description: Neutral fermentation end product of the acetolactate route from pyruvate, and the boundary the trait is named for. Butane-2,3-diol is one step further and is not curated: its dehydrogenase group K00004 is broad and is absent from several genomes that carry the acetolactate decarboxylase, so acetoin is where the evidence stops.

name: GTP
description: Purine nucleotide that supplies the pyrimidinedione ring of riboflavin and the pterin ring of folate. Input-only: guanylate biosynthesis is curated to GMP, and the phosphorylation between them is shared metabolism gifter does not curate.

name: D-ribulose 5-phosphate
description: Pentose phosphate intermediate that supplies the four-carbon unit of the riboflavin xylene ring.

name: riboflavin
description: Vitamin B2, and the boundary at which flavin identity is established. The kinase and adenylyltransferase that make FMN and FAD from it are shared housekeeping and are not curated.

name: chorismate
description: Aromatic branchpoint that leaves shikimate metabolism for 4-aminobenzoate and for menaquinone.

name: 4-aminobenzoate
description: Vitamin-adjacent boundary metabolite: the aromatic half of folate, separately synthesised, separately auxotrophic, and separately salvaged.

name: (6S)-5,6,7,8-tetrahydrofolate
description: Vitamin B9 in the reduced form that carries one-carbon units. Output boundary of folate biosynthesis.

name: 5-amino-1-(5-phospho-beta-D-ribosyl)imidazole
description: Purine pathway intermediate that ThiC rearranges into the thiamine pyrimidine. Declared here as an input boundary only; it is never an output anchor, so it creates no edge from purine biosynthesis.

name: 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate
description: Isoprenoid and thiamine precursor supplying the thiazole carbon skeleton and, in the DXP-dependent route, the pyridoxine ring.

name: 4-amino-2-methyl-5-(diphosphooxymethyl)pyrimidine
description: Activated thiamine pyrimidine moiety; the branchpoint where de novo synthesis and precursor salvage converge.

name: 4-methyl-5-(2-phosphooxyethyl)-thiazole
description: Activated thiamine thiazole moiety; the second convergence point of de novo synthesis and salvage.

name: thiamine phosphate
description: Vitamin B1 as the phosphate ester. The boundary stops here rather than at thiamine diphosphate because the ThiL kinase is unevenly annotated and its absence is an annotation gap rather than an auxotrophy.

name: 4-amino-5-hydroxymethyl-2-methylpyrimidine
description: Free thiamine pyrimidine, acquired from the environment and phosphorylated by salvage.

name: 5-(2-hydroxyethyl)-4-methylthiazole
description: Free thiamine thiazole, acquired from the environment and phosphorylated by salvage.

name: 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate
description: Branched-chain 2-oxo acid shared with valine biosynthesis; the carbon skeleton of pantoate.

name: (R)-pantothenate
description: Vitamin B5. The boundary stops here: the five steps that convert it to coenzyme A are shared housekeeping.

name: D-ribose 5-phosphate
description: Pentose phosphate intermediate; the ring precursor of the DXP-independent route to pyridoxal 5-phosphate.

name: D-erythrose 4-phosphate
description: Pentose phosphate intermediate; the entry point of the DXP-dependent route to pyridoxal 5-phosphate.

name: pyridoxal 5'-phosphate
description: Vitamin B6 in its catalytically active form, which is also the product of both biosynthetic routes, so no separate activation step exists to exclude.

name: pimeloyl-CoA
description: Seven-carbon dicarboxylic thioester that supplies the biotin valeric acid side chain. The marker layer does not distinguish it from the acyl-carrier-protein thioester used by the BioC/BioH route, so the anchor names the CoA form and the claim covers both.

name: biotin
description: Vitamin B7, the carboxyl carrier cofactor of acetyl-CoA and pyruvate carboxylases.

name: quinolinate
description: Committed pyridine precursor of NAD, and the point at which de novo synthesis is separated from salvage.

name: nicotinate D-ribonucleotide
description: Nicotinate mononucleotide: the junction where de novo quinolinate chemistry, nicotinate salvage and cobamide lower-ligand attachment all meet.

name: NAD(+)
description: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, the product that makes a genome independent of exogenous niacin.

name: nicotinate
description: Vitamin B3 as acquired from the environment; the input boundary of pyridine salvage.

name: uroporphyrinogen III
description: Tetrapyrrole branchpoint. Heme, siroheme and the corrin ring all leave shared metabolism here, which is why the cobalamin claim starts at this molecule and not earlier.

name: cob(II)yrinate a,c diamide
description: Completed, cobalt-loaded corrin ring. Both the aerobic and the anaerobic ring routes converge here, and everything after it is shared by de novo synthesis and corrinoid salvage.

name: adenosylcobinamide phosphate
description: Adenosylated corrinoid carrying its aminopropanol arm, ready for lower-ligand attachment. This is the molecule a corrinoid salvager imports and remodels.

name: 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole
description: The lower ligand that makes a cobamide into vitamin B12. A genome that assembles the nucleotide loop without it makes a different cobamide, which is not the vitamin.

name: adenosylcobalamin
description: Vitamin B12 in its coenzyme form, complete with the dimethylbenzimidazole lower ligand.

name: menaquinone
description: Vitamin K2. The terminal curated reaction is written on the quinol couple, as Rhea writes it; the anchor names the vitamin.

name: FMNH2
description: Reduced flavin mononucleotide, consumed rather than recycled by BluB, which dismantles it to build the benzimidazole ring. Declared input-only: it is the one cofactor in this layer that a reaction destroys.

name: oxaloacetate
description: Four-carbon junction connecting citric acid cycle chemistry, anaplerosis, gluconeogenesis and the aspartate family. Declared as both an input and an output of the cycle segments because the ring closes through it.

name: 2-oxoglutarate
description: The largest carbon-nitrogen junction in bacterial metabolism: the ammonium acceptor of glutamate synthesis and, through glutamate, the amino donor of most transaminations.

name: succinate
description: Boundary of citric acid cycle chemistry, of the Wood-Werkman route to propionate and of tetrapyrrole synthesis through succinyl-CoA. gifter makes no claim that a genome releases succinate; that trait is refused in inst/doc/proposal-organic-acid-formation.md section 6.4.

name: fumarate
description: Oxidised partner of the succinate/fumarate couple. gifter models no electron acceptors, so this anchor supports no fumarate respiration claim, and it is deliberately not attached to the purine or pyrimidine GIFTs whose routes involve fumarate as a co-product.

name: phosphoenolpyruvate
description: Glycolytic intermediate and the C3 donor of the shikimate pathway, consumed twice: once by the DAHP synthase condensation with erythrose 4-phosphate and once by the EPSP synthase transfer. Declared as an input boundary only; nothing in gifter produces it yet.

name: salicylate
description: 2-hydroxybenzoate. In bacteria it is a chorismate-derived siderophore building block, incorporated into pyochelin, yersiniabactin and mycobactin; in plants it is a defence hormone. The anchor names the free acid, which is where the curated chemistry stops: the salicyl-AMP ligase that commits it to a siderophore is a separate capability.

name: L-tryptophan
description: Aromatic amino acid and a branchpoint in its own right: the precursor of indole-3-acetate, of indole, of the kynurenines and of tryptophan-derived alkaloids, as well as a protein building block. Declared so that indole-3-acetate biosynthesis is not bundled with aromatic amino acid biosynthesis.

name: (indol-3-yl)acetate
description: The auxin. Bacterial production is a plant-interaction trait rather than a growth requirement, and the anchor is the free acid; conjugation to amino acids or sugars is not curated.

name: ammonium
description: Convergence point of every nitrogen-liberating capability and the entry point of assimilation. Declared under the nitrogen-anchor rule: ammonium is an anchor only where a reaction exists to liberate or assimilate it, never where it is a leaving group of chemistry aimed at something else. Three of the four curated reactions that mention it are therefore excluded; see database_changes.

name: nitrate
description: Environmental inorganic nitrogen source. Input-only, and deliberately compartment-unresolved: the specific NrtABCD importer covers 1582 genomes but the commoner NarK/NRT2 carrier is shared with nitrite and with respiratory contexts, so no transporter licenses a split. Supports no nitrate respiration claim; gifter models no electron acceptors.

name: urea
description: Host- and diet-derived nitrogen source, and independently the product of allantoin and creatinine degradation. The layer's clearest shared boundary. Compartment unresolved: three unrelated transport mechanisms carry it, two of them passive channels, and urea also arises intracellularly.

name: urate
description: Host purine end product and the entry point of ureide catabolism. This is the species RHEA:21368 itself uses, although ChEBI displays it under its systematic name.

name: (S)-allantoin
description: Branchpoint of purine nitrogen catabolism: released by urate degraders and consumed by the 774 genomes that degrade it while carrying no uricase of any kind. The clearest cross-feeding boundary in the database outside sugars.

name: glyoxylate
description: Carbon fate of allantoin degradation. It remains an output-only boundary: the glyoxylate bypass produces and consumes glyoxylate internally, so declaring an input edge would misstate the boundary of that complete route.

name: sarcosine
description: Convergence point of betaine and creatinine catabolism, and the reason both are cut here. Its own demethylation is commoner than either upstream capability, so curating betaine-to-glycine and creatinine-to-glycine separately would duplicate the same reaction in two GIFTs.

name: glycine betaine
description: Diet- and host-derived osmolyte, and the product of carnitine catabolism through the betainyl-CoA route. Declared as both an input and an output boundary of different GIFTs, which is what makes carnitine reach glycine by composition.

name: (R)-carnitine
description: Animal-tissue- and host-derived quaternary amine. Two curated capabilities consume it and they release different products, which is why they are separate GIFTs rather than two routes of one.

name: creatinine
description: Host muscle metabolite. Input-only.

name: trimethylammonium
description: Released product that the producing organism does not use and that the host converts to trimethylamine N-oxide. Output-only. A positive call means the chemistry is encoded, not that trimethylamine is produced, released, or reaches a host.

name: methylammonium
description: Environmental and microbially derived methylated amine. Input-only.

name: taurine
description: Host-derived aminosulfonate, released outside the cell by bile-salt hydrolases acting on taurine-conjugated bile acids. Split from the cytoplasmic form because TauABC is a specific and complete ABC importer, the same licence used for xylose and arabinose.

name: taurine
description: Taurine in the cytoplasm, where both curated desulfonation capabilities begin.

name: sulfite
description: Product boundary of taurine desulfonation. Assimilatory sulfate reduction passes through sulfite internally on its way to sulfide; dissimilatory sulfite reduction remains outside this GIFT.

name: L-glutamate
description: The nitrogen a cell can actually build with, and the sink that keeps ammonium from being a terminal boundary. Declared for ammonium assimilation only; glutamate metabolism generally is not curated, and reactions elsewhere that consume it internally gain no edge from it.

name: benzoate
description: Aromatic monocarboxylate. A plant secondary metabolite and a food preservative, and the compound most aerobic peripheral aromatic routes converge on before the ring is opened.

name: catechol
description: The dihydroxylated ring that aerobic ring cleavage acts on. Several peripheral routes converge here, which is why it is a boundary rather than an internal intermediate.

name: 3-oxoadipate
description: Product of ortho ring cleavage and lactone hydrolysis. It is no longer aromatic, and it exists only because a ring was opened.

name: 3-oxoadipyl-CoA
description: The CoA thioester where the ortho-cleavage funnel and the aerobic phenylacetate route meet, one thiolysis short of central metabolism.

name: 2-oxopent-4-enoate
description: Product of meta ring cleavage and of extradiol cleavage of dihydroxyphenylpropanoate. Rhea writes the downstream hydratase on the enol tautomer, (2Z)-2-hydroxypenta-2,4-dienoate; the anchor is the molecule, not one tautomer.

name: succinyl-CoA
description: Central metabolite. Introduced here as the exit of the aromatic funnel, and available to the citric acid cycle segments if they are ever cut at this node.

name: phenylacetate
description: Product of phenylalanine fermentation and a substrate for aerobic CoA-dependent ring degradation.

name: 3-phenylpropanoate
description: Dietary phenylpropanoid, also produced by gut fermentation of plant polyphenols. trans-Cinnamate is the same enzyme's other substrate and is deliberately not a separate anchor; see the GIFT description.

name: 3-(3-hydroxyphenyl)propanoate
description: Meta-hydroxylated phenylpropanoid, the second entry into the same ring-cleavage node.

name: 3-(2,3-dihydroxyphenyl)propanoate
description: Catecholic phenylpropanoid where the two entry routes converge, and the substrate of extradiol cleavage.

name: anthranilate
description: 2-Aminobenzoate. A tryptophan catabolite of both host and microbial kynurenine metabolism, and a peripheral entry into the catechol node.

name: phenol
description: Product of microbial tyrosine fermentation and an industrial compound; hydroxylated to catechol in one step.

name: L-alanine
description: Stable amino acid product of pyruvate transamination or reductive amination.

name: L-asparagine
description: Stable amino acid product; the amidated form of aspartate.

name: meso-2,6-diaminopimelate
description: Branchpoint where the four diaminopimelate routes converge. It is both the immediate lysine precursor and the peptidoglycan cross-link residue of most Gram-negative and many Gram-positive walls, which is why the layer cuts here rather than at lysine.

name: L-lysine
description: Stable amino acid product of diaminopimelate decarboxylation.

name: 2-oxobutanoate
description: Branchpoint 2-oxo acid that commits carbon to isoleucine. Reached by threonine deamination or by the citramalate route, and released again by methionine gamma-lyase, so it is the point where three otherwise unrelated capabilities meet.

name: L-valine
description: Stable amino acid product of branched-chain transamination.

name: L-leucine
description: Stable amino acid product of the isopropylmalate chain extension.

name: L-isoleucine
description: Stable amino acid product of the isoleucine branch of the acetohydroxyacid pathway.

name: L-phenylalanine
description: Stable aromatic amino acid product of the prephenate dehydratase branch.

name: L-tyrosine
description: Stable aromatic amino acid product of the prephenate dehydrogenase branch.

name: L-histidine
description: Stable amino acid product of the ten-step pathway from PRPP.

name: L-proline
description: Stable amino acid product of glutamate cyclisation and reduction; also the substrate of Stickland proline reduction.

name: L-ornithine
description: Branchpoint of the glutamate family: the arginine precursor, the product of the arginine deiminase pathway, and the polyamine precursor. Declared with an unspecified compartment; the arginine/ornithine antiporter makes it a compartment-split candidate once transport is curated.

name: L-arginine
description: Stable amino acid product, and the substrate of the arginine deiminase pathway.

name: 4-aminobutanoate
description: Decarboxylation product of glutamate; a fermentable substrate for other community members and a neuroactive compound in the host gut.

name: indole
description: Released tryptophan catabolite. It is an aryl hydrocarbon receptor ligand and an interspecies signal, and it is the molecule the classical clinical indole test detects.

name: methanethiol
description: Released volatile sulfur compound of methionine catabolism.

name: acetyl phosphate
description: Sole product of the Stickland glycine reduction and the phosphate donor of substrate-level ATP synthesis. Declared as a boundary because a metabolic GIFT must state one and glycine reductase has no other product; acetate interconversion continues to hold the same molecule internally, so the two do not connect until that GIFT is re-cut.

name: 5-aminopentanoate
description: Released end product of Stickland proline reduction.

name: D-threo-isocitrate
description: Central branchpoint exposed so the oxidative decarboxylation and glyoxylate bypass are separately composable without duplicating citrate synthase and aconitase.

name: dinitrogen
description: Atmospheric dinitrogen at the boundary of nitrogen fixation. The unspecified compartment records no localisation or environmental availability claim.

name: sulfate
description: Inorganic sulfur source at the boundary of assimilatory sulfate reduction. The unspecified compartment records no uptake claim.

name: L-ectoine
description: Compatible-solute product of the EctABC route. Declaring it as an output does not claim accumulation, export or osmotic protection.

name: heme b
description: Iron porphyrin product at the end of the protoporphyrin and coproporphyrin route families. It is distinct from siroheme and downstream heme derivatives.

name: 2,3-dihydroxybenzoate
description: Catecholate branchpoint between chorismate-derived head synthesis and enterobactin or other siderophore assembly.

name: enterobactin
description: Cyclic catecholate siderophore product. The boundary does not assert secretion, metal binding in situ or uptake.

name: choline
description: Quaternary ammonium precursor of glycine betaine. The unspecified compartment records no uptake or environmental-availability claim.

name: siroheme
description: Iron isobacteriochlorin cofactor and branchpoint product of siroheme biosynthesis. Declaring it does not imply cofactor incorporation, reductase activity, sulfur or nitrogen metabolism, or conversion through the alternative heme pathway.
